summary.headline: 3i Infotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4.1% YoY to ₹182 crore; H1 EBITDA margin ~7% with ₹2 crore operating cash flow.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about ₹182 crore, up roughly 4.1% YoY and 2.3% QoQ, with H1 revenue near ₹360 crore (+4.2%). Q2 EBITDA was ₹13.7 crore (7.5% margin) and PAT ₹6.7 crore; H1 EBITDA was ₹25.2 crore and PAT ₹13.2 crore, though year-ago figures included about ₹27 crore of one-time US ERC credit, so comparisons are not like-for-like. Management reorganised the business into three capability-aligned service lines from October 2026 and said modest growth should accelerate over the next two to three quarters. Legacy matters (e-Mudhra, RailTel arbitration, RBI/FEMA, inter-company balances) remained open.

segments.name: Digital Engineering Services (formerly Application, Automation & Analytics)
segments.commentary: Largest unit at ~74.1% of H1 FY27 revenue; covers application engineering and modernisation, enterprise apps, data and analytics, intelligent automation and quality engineering.

segments.name: Cloud Infrastructure & Security Services (formerly Infrastructure Services)
segments.commentary: ~17.9% of H1 FY27 revenue; focus on hybrid cloud, cybersecurity, digital workplace, enterprise automation and AI operations.

segments.name: Business Process Services
segments.commentary: ~7.8% of H1 FY27 revenue; management flagged headwinds from AI-driven automation and BFSI regulatory tightening in India.

segments.name: Geography: US / India / Middle East / APAC
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue split: US ₹89.4 crore (~49.1%), India ₹63.6 crore (~34.9%), Asia Pacific ₹4.5 crore; Middle East ₹24.5 crore, up 54.3% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: No numeric revenue guidance for H2 FY27 or FY28; management said momentum should continue from H1 levels.
Management expects modest growth to accelerate over the next two to three quarters, with growth focus on AI-led platforms, cybersecurity, cloud and automation.
Wage increase effective 1 October 2026 will raise wage costs from Q3 FY27; management said it will be absorbed without impact on EBITDA or PAT.
e-Mudhra decision on whether to pursue or drop the claim (claim made public at over ₹100 crore) expected within about four weeks; no P&L impact expected from either path.
RailTel arbitration expected to take one to two more quarters before exposure can be assessed; base claim already provided for.
capex_capacity: Setting up a separate subsidiary for AI, analytics and automation CoEs, approved by the Board; partnerships possible later.
Right-of-use assets rose in H1 due to a new 5-year lease for one location.
Rights issue completed October 2025; proceeds used for building CoEs, with part parked in FDs and bonds.
Working capital of over ₹20 crore invested in new contracts in India and Middle East during H1.
Over 150 data and advanced analytics professionals and 350 certified automation and quality engineering specialists; 12 specialised CoEs plus 2 corporate CoEs.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 added 25 new clients across banking, insurance, energy, manufacturing, government, consumer and technology.
Middle East revenue grew 54.3% QoQ to ₹24.5 crore on new business; new geographies Canada and East Africa added last quarter.

DSO rose because about ₹20 crore of receivables from two Middle East and a few Indian opportunities (built up late July to early August 2026) was outstanding at September end; management expects normalisation as collections start in Q3.
Management is building a new GCC sales sub-team, as it currently lacks expertise in the segment.
Management said it has no specific ESG strategy; EnGRC is a small governance, risk and compliance workflow tool.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth is expected in H2 FY27 and FY28, and what are the growth catalysts for Vision 2030?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric outlook given; management said growth would accelerate over two to three quarters, with focus on AI platforms, cybersecurity, cloud and automation. FY26 was a deliberate clean-up of loss-making businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Constant-currency growth, DSO increase, tax provision and FX hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency growth is not currently published but may be added. DSO rise was due to ~₹20 crore of receivables from late-period opportunities. India has large carried-forward losses; US tax provided with auditors. No FX hedging, as US revenue and roughly 70% of costs are in USD.

qa_highlights.question: Legacy issues: are they resolved, and what is the cash exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: RBI/FEMA settlement application still pending with RBI. Inter-company legacy balances in some entities run to ~₹900-1,000 crore, provided for where not recoverable; no top-ups needed in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowings rise while cash is ₹70-75 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Month-end overdrafts against FDs and bonds are used to meet salaries and repaid in the first week of the next month to avoid breaking FDs. Average borrowing is ~20% of the balance-sheet figure. US credit line fluctuates with US profits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the e-Mudhra matter and RailTel arbitration?
qa_highlights.answer: EOW deemed the complaint not criminal, at best civil. Decision on pursuing or dropping the claim (over ₹100 crore) within about four weeks. RailTel arbitration in witness stage; base claim already provided, with possible additional interest or costs not expected to be large.

qa_highlights.question: Which industries are targeted, and how is differentiation achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is BFSI, telecom, IT companies, retail, healthcare and logistics, varying by geography. Differentiation is building industry SME depth; management said it is not a unique differentiator versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the robotics/automation exposure and GCC business share?
qa_highlights.answer: No production robotics; focus is back-end process automation. GCC is a new segment with no major presence yet; a separate sales sub-team is being built.

risks_watch: Revenue growth remains modest (~4%); management has not quantified H2 or FY28 targets.
Open legacy items: RBI/FEMA settlement pending, inter-company balances of ~₹900-1,000 crore, and e-Mudhra and RailTel proceedings.
Wage hike from Q3 FY27 is a cost headwind that management says will be absorbed.
DSO elevated at September 2026 end; collections on ~₹20 crore of receivables are expected from Q3.
Business Process Services faces AI-driven and BFSI regulatory headwinds.
Management did not provide constant-currency growth; no FX hedging in place despite USD-dependent exposure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the transformation narrative and near-term momentum, but evasive on forward numbers and on constant-currency growth. Candid about legacy issues being slow to resolve, with several items still pending.
key_quotes: We are done with the base work of building capabilities and execution and now, as we move into the second half of FY27, our focus is on building business momentum, expanding our market presence, and driving sustainable profitable growth.
Now we have started seeing modest growth and expect it to accelerate over the next two to three quarters.
There is no financial implication of this because there was no claim from their side. It was our claim and which we have not accounted for.
